title: Asiya in Pharaoh's house
hookLine: Pharaoh's wife, who kept faith in the harshest house (66:11)

cards: A hard address for a person of faith: not a desert, not a prison, but a palace. The palace of the man who declared himself lord most high, who had the baby boys of a whole people killed.
And inside it, married to him, a woman who believed. The Qur'an calls her only the wife of Pharaoh. Tradition gives her the name Asiya.
She first appears when a chest is pulled out of the river.

teach.b: Surah al-Qasas tells it. Pharaoh's household pulls a baby out of the river, the baby Musa.

In a house that kills boys, his wife speaks first: he'll be a comfort of the eye for me and for you, don't kill him; maybe he'll be useful to us, or we'll take him as a son. Her first recorded words save a prophet's life.
In surah sixty-six she speaks again, and this time it's a prayer.

teach.h: BUILD ME A HOME WITH YOU.
teach.b: In Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Build for me a home with Thee in the Garden." She goes on to ask to be saved from Pharaoh and his deeds, and from a wrongdoing people.
The Qur'an sets her up as an example for all believers, and in the next verse sets Maryam beside her: one in a palace, one under a palm.

Notice the order of her words in Arabic: rabbi-bni li 'indaka baytan fil-jannah. 'Indaka, with You, comes before baytan, a house. Some scholars sum that detail up with an old saying: the neighbor before the house.
What happened to her, the Qur'an doesn't say. Commentators tell stories of her suffering for her faith; those come from later reports, not from the verse.
What the hadith does say, in al-Bukhari, is that many men reached perfection, but among women only Maryam and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh. The Qur'an never shows her leaving that house.
It shows her keeping her faith inside it, and saving a child while she was there.

how: Muslims honor Asiya, with Maryam, as a woman the hadith says reached perfection; her prayer in 66:11 is learned and recited as a du'a, including in hardship.

o: a queen who ruled a rich kingdom by the sea
Musa's mother, who set him on the river
Pharaoh's believing wife, who saved baby Musa

games.q: Asiya in Pharaoh's house — tap the pairs.
p: build for me a home with Thee

s: it calls her the wife of Pharaoh; the name Asiya comes from tradition.
her first recorded words saved Musa's life
don't kill him, he'll be a comfort of the eye (28:9).
a hadith names her among the most perfect women
al-Bukhari: among women, Maryam and Asiya.

games.q: you're in Pharaoh's palace. a baby boy is pulled from the river, and boys are being killed. what does Pharaoh's wife do?
o: asks them not to kill him, and to keep him.
sends him back down the river.
games.why: she speaks first: a comfort of the eye for me and for you, don't kill him (28:9). a believer's first act in the harshest house.

practice: Think of the place in your life that's hardest to be good in, a job, a family table, a group chat, somewhere you can't simply walk out of.

Ask what one small thing you could protect there, the way Asiya protected a baby: a kind word, a boundary, a quiet prayer, someone weaker than you. If you pray, you can say her line: my Lord, build for me a home with You.

wordCard.voice: Asiya. Pharaoh's believing wife, who saved the baby Musa and prayed for a home with Allah, with You before the house. Today's word.

orig.s: رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ
orig.note: Arabic, 66:11: my Lord, build for me, with You, a house in the Garden.

carryVoice: Your line: faith in pharaoh's house. With You first, then the house. See you tomorrow.
